# The First Star

Long ago, when the world was young and darkness ruled the night, there lived a weaver named Selene who possessed an extraordinary gift. Her threads shimmered with captured sunlight, glowing faintly even after sunset.

One winter, darkness lasted longer than ever before. The sun barely rose, and people grew fearful. Selene worked tirelessly, weaving a magnificent tapestry that held all the light she had ever captured. As she wove the final thread, she whispered a prayer: "Let there be light when darkness falls."

The moment she finished, the tapestry lifted from her hands and soared into the sky. Higher and higher it climbed, until it reached the heavens. There, it transformed—each golden thread becoming a point of brilliant light.

The first stars were born that night.

Selene watched in wonder as her creation scattered across the darkness, forming patterns and pathways. Though she had given away all her captured light, the stars shone down upon her, and she understood: her gift had become eternal.

From that day forward, whenever night falls, the stars remind us that even the smallest light, when shared, can illuminate the entire world. And weavers still whisper prayers of gratitude to Selene, the mother of stars.
